children.text: Born and raised in India, Abhishek has been a resident of San Ramon, California since 2007. In 2017, he started learning art at a local art studio, and has continued to pursue his passion for painting, using acrylics and oils. Abhishek enjoys all forms of painting, but generally leans towards realistic painting techniques. He is particularly drawn towards portraits and human subjects. He posts his work online under the pseudonym — ArtOfShek.
Artist. Technologist. Dad. Husband. Learner
I am just a painter who is in pursuit of being an Artist.

Emigrated in early teens from India after moving around in US like almost all immigrants, finally settled in beautiful Tennessee Valley of North Alabama. Happily married with two sons and working along my husband, yet art is where my journey begins and continues on. Even when it appeared that my path was not leading me to art yet all along it was propelling me towards it. I was submerged into family, friends, work, community; yet my creative passage whether it was in paint, clay or words always stayed on course. I am pretty much self taught artist, my work vibrates with my thoughts and feelings; it is a journal of my heart.

In past years I have taken on art challenges such as finishing 100 paintings in a year successfully as fundraiser for our local temple. Have done various solo and group exhibitions in North Alabama, taken my work cross country for entire exhibitions to raise fund for cause for the school of underprivileged children in India. Also, done large scale paintings which are now part of the public areas different institutions. Been featured on APT and APR several times, am proud recipient of grants of Alabama State Council on Arts and several awards for my paintings and clay sculptures. However, my last exhibition of 2022 "Moments of Radiance" and Darshan: Visions of India changed my direction of my work. Now, I am in pursuit of "that" spiritual experience through my work and I want it to be for the viewer of my work also.

I feel blessed that God has granted me the heart of an artist. He's given me nurturing, and supportive family, and surrounded me with valuable friends also wonderful community in North Alabama. I feel extremely lucky to have the opportunity of combining the cultural ideals of the two vastly different free nations: one of my ancestors and the one of my family's future. and am proud Indian American.

Biplab is a silicon valley based technology professional and an avid art enthusiast. Biplab's art focuses on contemporary socio political situations, both internation and national. He also loves to express human emotions through art. So a significant number of Biplab's art are portraits. His preferred medium is oil, pencil and soft-pastel. Biplab lives with his wife and 8 year old son in Milpitas, California. Apart from painting, he is also interested in the art and science of astrophotography.

name: Charmaine Hussain
roleTitle: SF Bay Area Mixed Media Artist
tagline: Mixed Media - paint, collage, gold leaf

children.text: I create abstract topographies of hope on canvas—maps of circular voids, rich with the possibilities of a better tomorrow.

I make paintings about belonging: who feels at home in the world, and who is still searching. I was born into a tight-knit, diasporic Muslim community shaped by a thousand years of continuous migration. My own life has led me through four countries, a geo-politically charged cross-cultural marriage, and the raising of a nonbinary child. This lived history drives my ongoing inquiry into belonging and its cost.

Luminous, biomorphic globes recur across my paintings, defiantly rooting in unlikely places. I work in mixed media — building layers of paint, collage, gold leaf — then scraping back and excavating until something essential emerges. Like the earthquake-prone land beneath my studio, my canvases crack and rebuild. Things fracture before they reform...sometimes with unexpected tendrils sprouting from the scar tissue. I paint as an act of healing: for myself and for anyone who has ever found themselves on the outside looking in.

I came to the USA to pursue a Stanford BA, followed by a Kellogg MBA and then spent fifteen years inside iconic American brands — Coca-Cola, Clorox, Kingsford, Hidden Valley, Nike — mastering how visual storytelling shapes identity and culture at scale. I carry that fluency into every mark I make in the studio.

My influences include Islamic geometric abstractions, Indus Valley cosmic symbols, Madhubani folk paintings, and Sufi mystic poetry, all of it circling the same question: what does it mean to belong. I am also inspired by the work of Hilma af Klint, S.H. Raza, Beatriz Milhazes, and Virginia Jaramillo. My paintings are held in private collections, and have also been exhibited in the Bay Area, New York, Los Angeles, and internationally in Hong Kong and Beijing.

I bring the same conviction to my canvases that I bring to my community. I serve on the boards of the Indian American Artists Association, Olive Hyde Art Guild, and PFLAG National, and am a strategic advisor to the boards of Narika and Desi Rainbow Parents. I have been invited to speak on the future of creativity on various podcasts, at Stanford University, and at Mastercard. My art and advocacy have also taken me to the White House as a guest of the president, and the United Nations in Geneva.
I started painting at 40 - after I exited my startup. And I'm in love.

I'm a technologist by day (Product executive at Salesforce), and have been featured on Forbes, SXSW, New York Times, Harvard Business School, Apartment Therapy and others over the years for both my creative and entrepreneurial work. I started painting as a way to slow down, fill the creative void since my startup.

Today my work explores two recurring themes. Some paintings are inspired by architecture and atmosphere—sunlit courtyards, weathered walls, hidden staircases, and places that feel suspended in time. Others focus on people—moments of reflection, conversation, creativity, and everyday rituals. Together, they form an evolving collection of contemporary paintings inspired by travel, thoughtful interiors, and the quiet beauty of ordinary life.
Every painting is created with the hope that it will become part of a home and be lived with for years to come.

name: Dipti Irla
tagline: Multi Media Collage from found objects

children.text: Dipti Irla is a fashion designer turned artist and has worked for well-known brands, both in India and the US. She currently resides in San Mateo, California where she received her graduate degree in Fashion Design from the Academy of Art University at San Francisco. Through the University program her final year work was selected to be displayed at the 2011 New York Fashion Week.

Her most recent corporate job was that of a technical designer with Stitch Fix. While she enjoyed her work, she sorely missed having a creative outlet. After the birth of her son in 2019 she decided to step away from the job and during that time started reconnecting with her creative side. This is when she decided to pursue art as a career.
At the heart of her art is a sense of playfulness, a spirit of joy that animates each and every piece I produce. In all of her work, she seeks to bring a message of positivity and hope.
The natural world and diverse cultural influences have long been a rich source of inspiration for her, with her upbringing in India infusing her work with elements of Indian art

Geeta Dave was born and grew up in India, where she absorbed the artistic traditions of her native country at the side of her father, the renowned artist Balvant Joshi. She received her Master's in creative painting from MS University in Baroda, India. Geeta Dave has lived in Baton Rouge, Louisiana for the last 36 years.

She is an artist, muralist, and art educator. Her paintings are filled with soft, poetic ancestral forms. Surreal images of humans are often integrated into parts of nature which represent her personal journey of life. Many of her paintings represent women and their ongoing struggles for identity and equality throughout the world.

She has completed many large scale murals and public art projects in her homeland of India and in Baton Rouge and other Louisiana cities. Included in her commissioned projects are The Life-U Mural Prism Group; Department of Defense Starbase Mars mural for their Youth Program; two projects for the Baton Rouge Coca Cola Company: their 100th Anniversary Project and for LSU Stadium, Coca-Cola Suite; Spanish and Native American culture mural for Louisiana Department of Culture, Recreation, and Tourism and Shreveport Regional Arts Council, Baton Rouge Green Our Light Has Come park project; and, fore murals for the Baton Rouge Zoo.

As an Art Educator, Geeta has been the director for many mural projects involving art students in Baton Rouge and its surrounding towns. These murals are now permanent displays in airports, libraries, schools, and downtown outdoor areas. She gives her best to her community and has received many honors and awards for her work with the students.
Geeta has had twenty art exhibits. They have been held in museums, art galleries, and universities in Alabama, New York, Illinois, Louisiana, and many cities in India.

She has been honored by thirteen awards for her art in the United States, India, Russia, and Switzerland. Among these distinguished honors are the Ford Foundation's National Performance Network Award, Arts Ambassador Award, Michael Crespo Visual Artist Fellowship Award by Cary Saurage, The Baton Rouge Arts Council, The Scholastic Art and Writing Golden Residency Award, and an Artist Residency at the Sam and Adele Golden Foundation in upstate New York.

name: Joyita Ghose
roleTitle: Founder of POSHAQ; Chairman of the Milpitas Arts Commission

children.text: For Joyita Ghose, painting on silk is more than a craft—it was a lifeline. At age 23, a near-death experience left her bedridden and facing a long, uncertain recovery. To pull her mind away from the "dreary existence" of hospital stays, her mother placed brushes, paints and fabric in her hands.

Though Joyita began as a self-taught artist—doodling in the margins of her childhood books in India—her recovery sparked a lifelong commitment to design. She went on to receive formal training in Fashion Design at West Valley College and the Brighton College of Technology, UK, later earning a degree in Graphic Arts from UCSC extension.

Joyita's designs are deeply personal "color stories" inspired by the intricate patterns of nature—flowers, butterflies, and clouds—and the ancient folk art of India, Africa, and South America. Using high-quality, wrinkle-resistant silk, gutta resist, silk dyes, and a professional twelve-hour steaming process, she ensures her vibrant pigments are permanent and washable.

Since 2005, POSHAQ has become a staple for women who want to feel special, different, and comfortable. Her work is recognized at the highest levels of American art and culture, featured in the Getty Museum, the De Young Museum, Asian Art Museum and the Legion of Honor gift stores.
Joyita is currently the Chairman of the Milpitas Arts Commission and is very involved in getting new murals, sculptures into the city to capture the diverse nature of Milpitas.
Ketaki, a former engineer, has transitioned into a self taught multi-media artist working with Alcohol inks, acrylic and watercolors.

Ketaki invites you to embark on a visual journey with her Alcohol ink creations featured on this page. The use of alcohol inks allows Ketaki to embrace serendipity, as the pigments blend and flow, creating unique patterns and textures. She often juxtaposes these ethereal and organic elements with the boldness and structure of acrylics and other paint media, to create visually captivating compositions.
Majella Pinto is a visual and literary artist, and also a Six Sigma Black Belt. She paints in oil and writes Fiction.

I am an artist based in Cupertino, California. Though I work with several mediums I now specialize in oil painting with a penchant for portraits. The human form and face interests me immensely and I love to observe people in natural settings. Through my paintings I like to look at people in different walks of life.

My paintings are on display at the Cupertino Library and at The Gallery House, Palo Alto. I have previously exhibited my art at several solo and group exhibitions in India. My painting titled 'The Wait' is on permanent display at The Indian Railway Institute of Financial Management (IRIFM) Secunderabad, India.
My painting "Lazy Afternoons" was selected for The de Young Open 2023 and was on display at The de Young Museum, San Francisco.

Neha Luhar-Trice is an artist living in Jacksonville, FL who holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree from the University of Illinois at Chicago. A Midwesterner by birth, relocation to the American Southeast in 2005 profoundly affected Neha's creative outlook.

Though trained as a photographer, her practice has expanded to include mixed-media collage utilizing primarily recycled papers and a mindful doodling technique called Zentangle. Neha's work has been selected for juried exhibitions nationwide, including shows in San Francisco, CA, Astoria, OR, and multiple appearances in the prestigious Krappy Kamera Exhibition at New York City's Soho Photo Gallery. She is currently working on a mixed media book exploring color and collage.

As an artist, my work explores the dynamic between imagination and what is visible to the eye. I aim to create portraits that challenge viewers to contemplate how gender and racial biases shape our perception of the world around us. Through my mixed media portraiture, I create visually striking and imaginative identities that also encourage critical reflection on the ways in which biases intersect and impact individuals' lives. My portraits represent imaginary people, shaped by their stories, emphasizing the idea that we are all unique individuals, more than what meets the eye.

My interest in the impact of post-colonialism on our world and art motivates me to use diverse media, including text, collage, and paint, to create multi-layered pieces that bridge imagination and reality. I seek to challenge conventional notions of identity and belonging by celebrating the diversity of my subjects and incorporating elements of their cultural heritage and history into my art.

I aim to inspire viewers to consider how gender and racial biases influence our society and encourage them to work towards dismantling systems of inequality. My art serves as a platform for dialogue and change, amplifying the voices and experiences of marginalized communities. Ultimately, my work is a medium for awareness, change, and a celebration of the resilience and triumphs of women and marginalized communities. I believe that seeing people from the heart, not just with the eyes, allows us to appreciate the richness of their stories and experiences.

I have been featured in publications and magazines such as Forbes, Maake magazine, Artmarket magazine and have exhibited in museums and galleries including the De Young Museum, San Francisco International Airport, UCSF Women's Hospital, San Mateo City Hall, San Mateo Library, Museum of Northern California, Gallery Route One and Brown University.

Born and raised in India, Pragati's art is steeped in folklore, history, and the grandeur of her cultural heritage. Armed with a background in Industrial Design and Architecture, she doesn't just paint - she engineers visual epics, crafting intricate narratives that hit you right in the soul.

Since 2020, she's been on an ambitious mission: reimagining the Ramayana like never before. Scouring over 15 ancient versions of the epic, written across centuries and languages, she unearths hidden gems - forgotten tales, surprising twists, and timeless lessons that deserve the spotlight. Through her Maximalist-Miniaturist style, she transforms each canvas into a cinematic experience, brimming with epic battles, undying love, and the kind of details that make you lean in closer.

And because a mere series of paintings, sculptures & installations isn't enough (go big or go home, right?), Pragati is now compiling this collection into a coffee table book - 75+ paintings packed with rare stories that will make you see the Ramayana in a whole new light.

name: Pragya Goel
tagline: Layered acrylic paintings with modeling paste and palette knives

children.text: Pragya Goel is a Mountain View–based textured abstract artist whose work explores the connection between memory, place, and material. Inspired by landscapes, travel, and personal experiences, she creates layered acrylic paintings using modeling paste and palette knives to build sculptural surfaces that invite viewers to slow down and look beyond the visible.

Working with a restrained palette and minimalist compositions, Pragya transforms familiar places into emotional landscapes. Rather than depicting scenes exactly as they appear, her paintings capture what remains after time has softened details—the feeling of home, the memory of a journey, or the quiet beauty found in nature.

Alongside her artistic practice, Pragya works as a software engineer, where precision and structure influence her creative process. This balance between order and intuition shapes each piece, blending thoughtful composition with expressive texture.
Through Embossed Impressions, she creates contemporary abstract works that encourage reflection and invite viewers to discover their own memories within the layers.

name: Purvi Shroff
tagline: Mixed media, fluid art, art journaling

children.text: I am a multidisciplinary mixed media artist with over twenty years of experience working across a variety of genres and mediums. Born and raised in India, I bring a rich cultural heritage into my work, which is further influenced by my time in Ohio and my current home in North Carolina.

Formally trained in Commercial Arts and Graphic Design, I enjoy blending digital elements with traditional techniques. My artistic style thrives on contrasts, by merging classical methods with contemporary themes, creating work that feels both grounded and fresh.

People, communities, and everyday surroundings constantly inspire me. I love experimenting with different media, surfaces, and scales believing that the boldest expressions often emerge from the smallest formats.

When I'm not working in mixed media, I'm either painting in fluid art or immersed in art journaling. I often switch between these styles, letting my intuition guide me. Each medium offers something different – fluid art allows for spontaneity and flow, while journaling gives me a more personal, reflective space to experiment and document inspiration.

In addition to exhibiting my work in galleries across Raleigh, Cary, Durham, and other parts of the U.S., I also create custom art commissions. Whether it's a personalized piece for a home, a unique gift, or a larger installation, I enjoy collaborating with clients to bring their vision to life through art.

My canvas is both my medium and my message—literally and figuratively. I paint what I see around me, drawing from my childhood memories and my life as a daughter, wife, mother, a newly minted grandmother, educator and artist. Each piece begins with charcoal scribbles, followed by splashes of color and lines that evolve as I work. I rarely plan ahead; the image emerges organically, guided by instinct and emotion.

My life's journey has deeply shaped me as an artist. Born and raised in India, I earned a fine arts degree in Chennai, where I was introduced to both Western and Indian art traditions. I developed a love for each and continue to move fluidly between Indian folk styles and modernist approaches such as Impressionism and Cubism—with equal flare.

Having lived in California for several decades, I am a fusion of both cultures, and that blend infuses my art. When I paint buildings, I think of the architect who envisioned them, the workers who built them, and the lives unfolding inside and beside them. Through every painting, I invite the viewer to look beyond the façade—to find a reflection of themselves and their own journey within the layers of color and form.

I'm Ramya Thattai, an artist with a passion to Indian tribal art that spans over two decades. Upon exploring various art forms from the Indian sub-continent, my heart finds its muse in the captivating realm of Madhubani art.
The joy of creating original Madhubani art is not only a personal delight but also extends to adorning living spaces of art lovers with my expressions of creativity.
The overwhelming appreciation from friends and family, coupled with their unwavering encouragement, has inspired me to unveil Hasya Arts, my online art store.

I craft Madhubani-inspired folk art that brings everyday moments to life through vivid storytelling. My original creations come to life on diverse natural canvases, be it paper, fabric, wood, terracotta, bamboo, and beyond.

My works are lyrical, spiritual, layered and flowing, revealing the stories of unity in diversity, hope and connection, celebration of earth and women. The common thread running through my work is that I am seeking oneness among humanity, soil and soul.

As an internationally exhibited woman artist I bring a unique global perspective due to the fact that I was born into the Sindhi and Hindu traditions in Rajasthan, India, and later embraced Islam and moved to USA in 1986. As a woman, artist, and mother, I work to create harmony by expressing the universality of humanity through paintings, sculpture, calligraphy and poetry. Inspired by the imagery, sculpture and writings of my Indian heritage and Islamic spirituality, I use my artistic voice to break down the barriers that divide to foster peace and understanding. At birth I was given the life-defining challenge of a left hand without fingers. Seeing the unity of an all-encompassing God, I was able to transcend the barriers often set-forth in the traditions of religion, culture, and the cultural perceptions of handicaps. I have tried to bring together Eastern spirituality and Western techniques of painting learned over the years. Through the contrasting elements in my work, I yearn and search for unity balance.

My works are greatly influenced by my studies and experiences in different cultures around the world. After graduating in Fine Arts from Maharaja Sayajirao University in Baroda, India, I lived and worked in Iran and Kuwait, where I was exposed to a wealth of Islamic arts and Arabic calligraphy. Calligraphy, miniatures, and the folk art of Islam and the Hindu tradition continue to influence my work today.

I was invited to Germany twice, first as a Resident Artist in 2000 at Schwabisch Gmund and again in the Spring of 2011, by the Westphalia Wilhelm University in Münster, Germany invited to publish my paper "Art Informed by Spirituality" in the publication on the International Symposium: 'God Loves Beauty: Post Modern Views on Religion and Art. I have presented my work and given talks at Stanford University, Commonwealth of San Francisco, Seattle University, Graduate Theological Union at Berkeley, and Museum of Contemporary Religious Art, St. Louis Missouri. I was invited to Morocco for a one-month Artist Residency Program in March of 2018 through Green Olives art Gallery.

As a visual artist I have had 45 solo shows nationally and internationally and have won several prestigious awards including the East Bay Community's Fund for Artists in 2012 and 2014 and 2020. The City of Berkeley's Individual Artist Grant Award in 2014, 2015, and 2016. I have public art pieces on display in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania and San Diego, California and I have also written and published five books on my art and poetry including my recent with ecological consciousness from Quranic verses "Our Earth: Embracing All Communities."

My story begins with a line and the lines that I create represent the spiritual energy that emanates from my soul. My method is a physical and meditative process that fills each canvas with moving lines and multi-layered textures. For me creating art means getting physically involved with the piece: scratching, sanding, layering materials like paper, rope, modeling paste, paper-mache or copper plate, and embroidering with pen and ink. I apply thin layers of acrylic color in between adding textures and this working process brings out subliminal images. I also paint with rust pastels, use jute twine rope on handmade Korean paper Hanji, and apply glaze to seal everything. In my studio mysteries are revealed each day and I feel awed and inspired to delve further into the unknown fearlessly and look out for new visions emerging on my canvas.

Saranya Chandrasekaran is an artist based in the San Francisco Bay area. With a background in engineering and a discerning eye for design, she passionately explores and innovates techniques that seamlessly blend her diverse expertise.

Saranya's artistic practice is motivated by the interplay of nature, science, memories, and identity. She strives to help audiences see the unseen—both literally and philosophically. Through paintings, drawings, and mixed media, she explores bold expressions of emotion and the subtleties of perception, often drawing inspiration from expressionism, impressionism, and experimental art.

Nature serves as her primary muse; she is captivated by the various layers that compose our visible and invisible world. This fascination sometimes leads her to incorporate technology into her work, allowing her to experiment and innovate in ways that deepen the viewer's experience.

Saranya hopes her artworks kindle a spark of curiosity, inviting viewers to pause and reflect on the beauty and complexity of life. She firmly believes that art enriches our existence, encouraging us to slow down and appreciate the finer details around us.
I am very impressed with Gandhiji's Truth and Non Violence, I painted many paintings of him. Trying to convey his message to world.

name: Shraddha Tiwari
tagline: Painting, mixed media, lens-based explorations, experimental film

children.text: I am multidisciplinary artist exploring storytelling through material, memory, and myth. My work draws inspiration from the rich visual traditions of Indian folklore, epics, and devotional imagery, which I reinterpret through experimental contemporary processes.

I work across painting, mixed media, and lens-based explorations, often incorporating unconventional materials and organic textures to build layered, tactile surfaces. My practice is deeply process-driven, allowing curiosity, movement, and material behavior to shape the final work. Themes of play, transformation, and cultural memory frequently appear in my work, where mythological references intersect with everyday observation.

I am particularly interested in how we see and experience images. Through experiments with light, liquid, color, and magnification, I create ephemeral visual worlds that blur the boundaries between painting, photography, and abstraction.

Alongside my studio practice, I am passionate about arts education and community engagement. I teach art to children and community groups in the San Francisco Bay Area, introducing them to Indian art traditions while encouraging experimentation, imagination, and creative confidence. I have worked extensively as an art educator and have also served as a Program Director, designing and leading creative programs that bring art, storytelling, and cultural exploration to diverse communities and young learners.
My work is an ongoing dialogue between heritage and exploration, where ancient stories, playful discovery, and material experimentation come together to form new visual narratives.

name: Smita Garg
roleTitle: Indian-American artist and Holistic Healer; Former Chair of San Jose Arts Commission; Board member of SVCreates
tagline: Traditional and folk Indian art with themes of peace, nature, and spirituality

children.text: Hi, I am Dr. Smita Garg, an Indian-American artist and Holistic Healer based in Bay area, CA. Welcome to my page!

My work highlights my inner spirituality and my connection with nature and Mother Earth. I have worked extensively with local environmental organizations on raising awareness about the need to protect nature preserves. I am the founder of the holistic healing enterprise, Kinder Way Healing (Kinderwayhealing.com), offering many healing modalities; I am a founding member of local artist-activist collective, Creatives for Compassionate Communities; and also the Co-founder of educational non-profit, Campbell High School District Ed Foundation which serves over 8000 students and 7 Bay area schools. I also teach mindfulness and self-care classes and have lead group workshops for the same for several Bay area based and national organizations.

Most recently I have served as Chair for San Jose Arts Commission and successfully completed my 7-year term on the commission. I have continued to serve the arts community via my role as board member on SVCreates, a prominent Bay Area non profit supporting the arts. In my personal art style, I have found synergy with traditional and folk Indian art, where themes related to peace, nature and spirituality are skillfully and intentionally woven into the artwork. My artwork is a reflection and synthesis of my love for art and my deeply spiritual inner world. In my art, I also like to convey my experience of being someone who is very comfortable in a multicultural world and who feels at home everywhere.
Dr. Smita Garg holds a BFA in Applied Art from College of Art (COA), New Delhi and a Doctorate in Arts Education from the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign.
I am a self-taught, award-winning eco feminist artist from Lalit kala Academy India.
I am a teaching artist and Open Source leader, with my studio at Milpitas.
I am an active docent and active continuing docent education chair at San Jose Museum of Art.
I am also the founder of president of Indian American Artists' Association (IAAA) – a non-profit helping Indian-origin artists in the US find a platform to show their art.
I have conducted solos around the globe including University of Illinois, Chicago, Lalit Kala Academy, New Delhi, and Jawahar Kala Kendra, Jaipur.

name: Swati Rastogi
tagline: Mixed media, mandalas, tribal art, murals, public art

children.text: From the time I remember, Art has always been my passion, driving me to a formal education that included my Bachelors in Fine Arts and Masters in History of Arts from India.
I have developed a style which involves my study, culture, traditions, aesthetics, emotions and intellect. Influences from folk and tribal arts of India consistently reflect in my creations.
I paint mandalas- a motif of completeness and integrity. The design begins from a circle and then gradually emanates to bigger and fuller pattern, keeping everything to one central point.
I also paint a lot of tribal art narratives of life and nature. Lately been experimenting some abstract compositions, textures and revisiting my much older themes.
I have lived a very artful life on the East Coast prior to moving to the Bay Area. I paint many mediums, murals and public art I enjoy the most.
I am an Indian-born San Francisco based artist and I create abstract paintings that distill the light, the intense colors, and the constant movement in nature.

Usha Shukla was born and brought up in New Delhi, India. From early childhood, she was fascinated by the outdoors. The vibrant colors of the Indian countryside left a strong impression on her. After a graduate degree in English Literature, she went on to get a diploma in Fashion Design. In 1996 when she moved to San Francisco, California, with her family, she found everything different except her interaction with nature. In 2005, after a visit to the Louvre Museum in Paris, she realized her true passion for art. She enrolled in the local community college and started her formal art education. She completed her graduate program at the Academy of Art University, San Francisco, focusing on painting.

Combining her love of nature and passion for art, she paints large abstract paintings in vibrant colors. She has a unique process of mark-making. Instead of conventional tools like brushes and palette knives, she moves the paint on wood panels using an air blower.

Her work is collected by several local art collectors. She won the 2016-17 Clyde & Co Art Award for Emerging Artists, San Francisco. She has participated in several juried group and solo shows on the West Coast and has won awards. She has a public art mural in the city of Livermore, California. Her six paintings are installed in the East County Hall of Justice, Dublin, CA, commissioned by the Alameda County Arts Commission. Five of her works are in the permanent collection at the Sutter Hospital in San Francisco and one in Boston Children's Hospital, Boston. She recently exhibited her work at Spectrum, Miami during the Miami Art Basel Week. She received the 2020 Alameda County Arts Leadership Award and now serves as an Art Commissioner on the Alameda County Arts Commission.

name: Vasu Tolia
tagline: Mixed media - acrylics, ink, charcoal, oil crayons, paper collage

children.text: I create paintings using mixed media - including acrylics, ink, charcoal, oil crayons and paper collage. I love the instant fulfillment that comes from completing an artwork. I strive to capture the moments, movements of the world and transfer these experiences and emotions into my paintings. My art is constantly evolving to morph from representational to subtle or absolute abstraction on various themes I explore. Although the word abstract means to separate or withdraw something from something else, its application in my art is based on a thought or a moment using shapes, colors, forms and gestural marks to achieve its effect. I hope to provoke curiosity and interest while permitting myself a sense of freedom of expression and give the viewers, a freedom of interpretation.

As I lay and play with the materials, I infuse my personality in it. I layer marks with charcoal, pastel, and ink with acrylic paint and/or medium with bands. Ultimately, intuition takes over, happy accidents can happen with brush during planned and unplanned moments. I become the willful maestro making the artwork march to my notes. I may show the brushstrokes or create an ethereal softness, leave hard edges or add texture. Eventually, collision of these in multiple layers creates an emotion, inviting the viewer to feel something real, imagined or both. Creating this hybrid of abstract exploration of nature vs. figure while blurring and keeping some boundaries gives me great joy.
